newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS BECOME LEAGUE'S FIRST 30-GAME WINNERS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS BECOME LEAGUE'S FIRST 30-GAME WINNERS.

text.p: Michael Jordan scored 33 points and Dennis Rodman pulled down 26 rebounds as the Chicago Bulls became the National Basketball Association's first 30-game winners this season with a 116-101 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday.
Toni Kukoc added 20 points, Scottie Pippen chipped in 19 and Rodman scored 16 to go with his season-high for rebounds for the defending NBA champions, who improved to 30-4.
Glenn Robinson scored 35 points, Vin Baker added 26 and rookie Ray Allen contributed 22 for the Bucks, who suffered their biggest loss of the season.
The Bulls out-rebounded the Bucks 45-33, including 21-7 on the offensive boards.
"Tonight was my night," Rodman said. "In the first half we got the cobwebs out, in the second half we kicked (butt)."
The Bucks led by 10 after the first quarter but the Bulls outscored Milwaukee 59-40 in the second half -- 30-18 over the final 12 minutes.
In Philadelphia, Clyde Drexler scored 31 points, Hakeem Olajuwon had 26 and Charles Barkley grabbed 25 rebounds as the Houston Rockets crushed the Philadelphia 76ers 120-99.
Barkley also scored 18 points for the Rockets, who have not lost to the 76ers in five years, a span of 11 games.
"We just played well from the beginning to end," said Barkley, whose Rockets have won six of their last eight games and improved to a league-best 15-2 on the road.
Jerry Stackhouse scored 26 points, while rookie Allen Iverson had 26 and 11 assists for Philadelphia, which has dropped eight games in a row and 18 of its last 19.
In Boston, Patrick Ewing had 31 points and 15 rebounds as the New York Knicks continued their dominance of the Celtics with a 111-98 victory in the opener of a home-and-home set.
The Knicks have won the last 16 meetings between the teams, including 10 straight at Boston.
John Starks added 18 points off the bench for the Knicks, who have not lost to the Celtics in four years.
The Celtics took their last lead at 86-85 with 6:57 to go, but Allan Houston's jumper ignited a 10-0 Knicks' run over the next 2:05.
Rick Fox led Boston with a season-high 26 points.

At Detroit, Grant Hill recorded 19 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists and Terry Mills added 18 points as the Pistons opened a big first-half lead and cruised to an 84-78 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

Mills made a three-pointer to cap a 25-5 run that gave the Pistons a huge 47-23 advantage with 4:07 remaining in the second quarter. Mills had 13 points during the run, including a trio of three-pointers.
Vernon Maxwell scored 21 points and Cory Alexander added 18 for the Spurs, who have lost four straight games following a season-high three-game winning streak.
In Phoenix, Wesley Person scored 27 points and pulled down a career-high 15 rebounds as the undermanned Suns downed the Charlotte Hornets 102-90.

Kevin Johnson added 20 points and 13 assists and Mark Bryant had 14 points for the Suns, who had only nine players available after trading Robert Horry and Joe Kleine to the Los Angeles Lakers earlier in the day.
Six of the nine players who played scored in double figures for the Suns, who snapped a five-game losing streak.
Glen Rice had 25 points and Anthony Mason added 17 points and 18 rebounds for the Hornets.
At Washington, Chris Webber's tip-in with 1:46 to play snapped a tie and Chris Whitney sank a pair of free throws with 3.6 seconds left as the Bullets edged the Los Angeles Clippers 102-98.
Webber finished with 25 points and Calbert Cheaney added 22 for Washington.

Rod Strickland and Juwan Howard each missed free throws in the final 21 seconds that could have put the game away for the Bullets. Los Angeles then blew a chance to tie the game when Eric Piatkowski missed a layup with four seconds left.
In Denver, Reggie Miller scored 18 points and Rik Smits and Antonio Davis added 16 apiece as the Indiana Pacers climbed back to the .500 mark with a 108-89 romp over the Nuggets.
Smits was starting just his second game of the season after missing the the first 30 following surgery on both his feet in September.
LaPhonso Ellis scored 14 points and Darvin Ham added 13 for the Nuggets, who have lost six of their last seven games and are a league-worst 4-13 at home.
In Los Angeles, Shaquille O'Neal had 34 points and Eddie Jones added 25 as the Lakers beat the Miami Heat 94-85 for their 11th straight home victory.
O'Neal had seven points during a pivotal 18-4 run by Los Angeles early in the fourth quarter and tied a personal best with his 26th consecutive game of at least 20 points.
Alonzo Mourning led Miami with 31 points while P.J. Brown and Tim Hardaway finished with 14 apiece.
